title: Evaluation-preserving local-Hom comparisons for twisted action-site restriction
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site with pullbacks, $s:C\simeq C$ continuous in both directions, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $a:(s^{-1})^*R\simeq R$, and $P$ a RestrictionPresentation [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data]. Write $D$, $A$, $U$, and $\sigma$ for its action site, coefficient ring, underlying module restriction and scalar-transported inverse translation. Fix normalized TensorComparisons $T$ [lem-sf-twisted-action-tensor-comparisons]. There exist isomorphisms $h_{M,N}:U\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\simeq\mathcal Hom_R(UM,UN)$ and $c_{L,K}:\sigma\mathcal Hom_R(L,K)\simeq\mathcal Hom_R(\sigma L,\sigma K)$, for all module sheaves on $D$ and $C$ respectively. They preserve evaluation with the tensor comparisons of $T$: $U(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})=t_{M,\mathcal Hom(M,N)}(1\otimes h_{M,N})\mathrm{ev}_{UM,UN}$ and $\sigma(\mathrm{ev}_{L,K})=b_{L,\mathcal Hom(L,K)}(1\otimes c_{L,K})\mathrm{ev}_{\sigma L,\sigma K}$, in diagrammatic order. These data form HomEvaluationComparisons. No action equation or naturality equation for $h$ is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the restriction Hom map explicitly as the transpose of inverse tensor comparison followed by restricted evaluation. The restriction-only canonical comparison theorem makes this map invertible; use asIso. It assumes no translation Hom data.

Construct the translation Hom map in the same way. P.translation_eq makes sigma an equivalence. For every Q, full faithfulness, the source tensor-Hom adjunction, full faithfulness again, the inverse sigmaTensor comparison, and the target tensor-Hom adjunction give a bijection from maps sigma Q to sigma Hom(M,N) to maps sigma Q to Hom(sigma M,sigma N). Naturality of sigmaTensor in the second factor identifies this bijection with postcomposition by the constructed map. Essential surjectivity extends bijectivity to every test object. The Yoneda isomorphism criterion proves the translation comparison invertible.

The inverse tensor-Hom equivalence sends f to (identity tensor f) followed by evaluation, by naturality in the tensor variable. Apply this to each canonical comparison. The inverse-equivalence identity and tensor comparison hom-inverse cancellation prove both evaluation equations. Package the two asIso isomorphisms with these equations. This proof keeps the original statement, including all universes and edge cases.

proof_origin.place: lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor; canonical evaluation mates, full faithfulness of translation, and the Mathlib isIso_of_yoneda_map_bijective argument. Restriction invertibility is isolated as a strictly smaller obligation.

theorem homEvaluationComparisons [HasPullbacks C] (P : RestrictionPresentation J s R a)
    (T : TensorComparisons J s R a P) :
    Nonempty (HomEvaluationComparisons J s R a P T)
